questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My previous experiences with that part of the world. Language requirements and covid-restrictions also played a big part.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I recall it as being easy. If you are in doubt email your contact person or the relevant teacher.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived a few weeks late due to covid related issues. Therefore I had other exchange students helping me out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was abit difficult to find something affordable. It is a good idea to look for accommodation as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Privacy and space are not cheep in Hong Kong. My best advise would be to find a roomate you get along with. It really helped me alot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid no exchange students got offered on campus accomodation. Check if that is the case for you too. If not you need to apply early to get a drom room.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Prepare to very flexible with what courses you are going to end up with.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was abit messy. First of you have to pre-select courses. I ended up getting half of those courses. The others were already filled, not offered for some reason or the course material was only partially in english. When the online registration opened up I found it hard to figure out what courses I was able to apply for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I cannot recall to be honest.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: About half I would say. I ended up just going for what I thought sounded interesting while being somewhat relevant.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seems your best shot at getting courses is through pre-registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did not find the courses difficult but there was a high work load with 5 courses at once.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More group assignments, multiple choice tests, and powerpoint presentations than I was use to. Being asked to rate the presentations of my fellow sutdents also felt abit unusual. That only happened in one course though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundamentals of Persuasive Communication
Fundamentals of Advertising
Cognitive Psychology
Media and Society
Architecture and Space in Chinese Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
In hindsight I would have picked different courses.
Fundamentals of Persuasive Commnication provided some insight in applied communication and arugmentation which I did apperciate. Fundamentals of Advertising touched upon a lot of the same things.
Media and Society felt abit like a repetition of other courses taught at Kommmunication og IT.
If you have any interest in Ancient Chinese Archtecture I would recommend that course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Doctor and hospital fees. These were very low however ( 200-300HDK ).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many groceries are pretty expensive. Because of that most exchange stundets I talked to also did not bother cooking at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were alot of societies and clubs, but I think you need to apply for those before the semester starts. There will also be events offered via your CityU Mail such as a one day archery course.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in latin dance there is after work Sala at Rula Live every monday at 8pm. Other thant that enjoy the city life and go hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It was not possible to visit Maccao or Shenzhen due to covid, otherwise I would have. Go camping with some friends on some of Hong Kongs remote islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy. I found it more liberal than mainland China. Just keep in mind that it is a bit city fast paced and crowded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it hard to get to know Hong Kong students. The best way seemed to be participating in some of the events. Joining hikes and social events is in general a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: When visiting small local resturents prepare to use pictures and practice a few phrases of Cantonese. It is a part of the experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the fact that Hong Kong is a mixture of Eastern and Western in a lot of ways. I am also a big fan of the local food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring money and more of it than you expected. 
Remember summer clothes for the hot days as well as clothes for the cold aircon at the library.
Do not forget to have a great time!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not on top of my head.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Not to sound cheesy but the friendships made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing my time! The day goes fast. Balancing a lot of courses, socializing and exploration can be though.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Hong Kong is great, the place has alot of variation! Big city life, small villages, beaches and mountain tracks all with 2 hours of transport.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
